Periodontal Care & Implants

Implants After Gum Disease

Had gum disease? You can still have implants. We treat the disease first, then restore your beautiful smile.

Free 15-Min Chat1-Hour Consultation — £80Call 020 71833573

✓ Periodontal Experience · ✓ Treat Then Restore · ✓ Long-Term Success

Gum disease, or periodontitis, is a silent but destructive condition. It often starts without pain but progressively destroys the soft tissue and bone that support your teeth.

When left untreated, the gums pull away from the teeth, creating infected pockets. The body's immune system fights the bacteria, but this response also breaks down the bone and connective tissue holding teeth in place. Eventually, teeth become loose and may fall out or need extraction.

At Dental Implants London, we understand the distress this causes. Our approach is two-fold: halt the disease to protect remaining teeth, and rebuild the lost foundation to support long-lasting dental implants.

The Path from Infection to Implant

You cannot build a house on shaky ground. Before we can restore your smile with implants, we must ensure the biological environment is healthy.

The Challenge

  • • Active infection (bacteria) can attack new implants (Peri-implantitis).
  • • Significant bone loss often accompanies gum disease.
  • • Gums may be recessed, affecting aesthetics.

The Solution

  • • Targeted hygiene therapy to stabilise the condition.
  • • Bone grafting to regenerate lost structure.
  • • Precision implant placement in healthy, sterile bone.

Our Protocol

Restoring Health & Function

We don't just fill gaps; we treat the person. Our protocol ensures that your new smile is built to last by addressing the root cause of your tooth loss first.

1

Stabilization & Hygiene

Our dental team deep cleans the gums to remove bacteria and calculus. We ensure the disease is inactive before surgery.

2

Bone Reconstruction

If gum disease has eroded your jawbone, we use advanced grafting materials to rebuild the height and width needed for implants.

3

Implant Placement

Once the foundation is solid, we place titanium implants. These integrate with your new bone, providing a stable anchor for crowns or bridges.

Stop the Cycle of Tooth Loss

Gum disease is often manageable with appropriate professional care. Early treatment may help protect your teeth and support long-term oral health.
